events.title: Deck the Hall | Christmas Tree Competition
events.description:
Get ready to deck the halls and show off your holiday creativity!

Deck the Halls is a festive Christmas tree decorating competition where teams, businesses, organizations, and community members can transform a Christmas tree into their own unique holiday masterpiece.

Decorate during the week of thanksgiving and take down is the first week of January. Choose a theme, gather your team, and let your imagination run wild! Whether your tree is traditional and elegant, hilariously over-the-top, or completely unexpected, we want to see what you can create. Then the community gets to vote! Every penny counts as a vote, and the tree with the most votes wins! The winning group get to choose a local nonprofit to receive ALL of the proceeds! Trees will be on display for the community to enjoy.

It’s a fun way to celebrate the holiday season, showcase local creativity, and bring a little extra Christmas magic to the community.

Think you have what it takes to take home the title?

Grab your ornaments, lights, garland, and your best decorating crew—and get ready to Deck the Halls!

Contact Sami at spettey@co.mckenzie.nd.us to enter, and the entry fee is $20.

events.title: Explore Theodore Roosevelt National Park
events.description:
Come explore Theodore Roosevelt National Park! Come experience the national parks! On six days each year, all National Park Service sites that charge an entrance fee will offer free admission to everyone. Mark your calendar for these entrance fee–free dates:

February 16, 2026: Presidents Day (Washington’s Birthday) May 25, 2026: Memorial Day June 14, 2026: Flag Day July 3–5, 2026: Independence Day ( https://www.nps.gov/subjects/npscelebrates/july4th.htm ) weekend August 25, 2026: 110th Birthday of the National Park Service ( https://www.nps.gov/subjects/npscelebrates/nps-birthday.htm ) September 17, 2026: Constitution Day October 27, 2026: Theodore Roosevelt’s birthday November 11, 2026: Veterans Day ( https://www.nps.gov/subjects/npscelebrates/veterans-day.htm )

National parks are America’s best idea, and there are more than 400 parks ( https://www.nps.gov/findapark/index.htm ) available to everyone, every day. The fee-free days provide a great opportunity to visit a new place or an old favorite, especially one of the national parks that normally charge an entrance fee ( https://www.nps.gov/planyourvisit/fee-free-parks-state.htm ). The others are free all the time. The entrance fee waiver for fee-free days does not cover amenity or user fees for activities such as camping, boat launches, transportation, or special tours. The annual $80 America the Beautiful National Parks and Federal Recreational Lands Pass allows unlimited entrance to more than 2,000 federal recreation areas, including all national parks that normally charge an entrance fee. There are also free or discounted passes available for senior citizens, current members of the military, families of fourth-grade students, and disabled citizens. Learn more about the variety of passes offered by the America the Beautiful National Parks and Federal Recreational Lands Pass ( https://www.nps.gov/planyourvisit/passes.htm ) series.

events.description:
Clay Sculpting Open Studio 👐✨ Join us for a hands-on Clay Sculpting Open Studio where creativity takes shape! Each person receives 1 pound of clay included in the $45 price, with the option to add extra clay for $10 per additional pound.

This is a hand-building experience only—no pottery wheel—just your hands, your imagination, and the tools we provide. Create anything you can dream up! Once your sculpture is complete, we’ll take care of the rest. Your piece will be professionally fired in our kiln, and when it’s ready, you’re invited to return during a Paint Your Own Pottery Open Studio to glaze your creation.

This experience is perfect for both kids and adults, whether you’re a beginner or a seasoned maker. All firings are included in the price, so you can focus on having fun and bringing your ideas to life.

✨ The ideas are limitless—come get your hands dirty and create something truly unique! ✨

events.title: Books & Banter: "The Cloak" by Nickolai Gogol
events.description:
“Books and Banter,” a monthly book club featuring Victorian-era literature, will meet Tuesday, Nov. 17, 9-10 a.m. at the Chateau de Morès Interpretive Center in Medora. Book selections are intended to be easy to read and fun to discuss. Coffee and tea will be provided.

This month’s book, “The Cloak” by Nickolai Gogol was originally written in Russian, one of the seven languages Medora von Hoffman spoke! The book tells the story of a quiet clerk whose life changes after he buys a new coat. The book is available to read for free via Project Gutenberg.

When the State Historical Society of North Dakota took possession of the Chateau de Morès, it held a library so extensive that locals would borrow its books. The subjects of these books range from poems to military tactics, early childhood education to romance novels, and animal husbandry to human medical care.

This event is part of the ND250 commemoration celebrating our country’s 250th birthday.

For more information, contact Outreach Coordinator Shelby Reidle, shschateau@nd.gov or 701.623.4355. The Chateau de Morès State Historic Site is managed by the State Historical Society of North Dakota. The Chateau de Morès Interpretive Center hours are Tuesday-Saturday, 9 a.m.-5 p.m., and closed Sunday-Monday. The home is open by appointment. All times listed are Mountain time. Find information about upcoming programs of the State Historical Society at history.nd.gov/events.

This event also serves as a forum for our seniors to present their senior capstone projects, which includes both an oral and poster presentation at the event. events.description:
Building: Student Center Room: Movie Theater Organizer: Badlands Film Appreciation Society Category: Clubs and Orgs,Community Events,Fine and Performing Arts,Student Activities Audience: Pu blic Cost to attend: Free Link: https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0093748/?ref\_=nv\_sr\_srsg\_0\_tt\_8\_nm\_0\_in\_0\_q\_planes%20trains

Of course, another key aspect of Thanksgiving is the feast, shared by loved ones as a sign of gratitude for surviving another year and being loved by others. While set in Denmark in the late 19th century, Babette's Feast \(1987, G\) fully captures that Thanksgiving spirit. The film presents the story of two elderly sisters who have tried to keep alive their father's ministry to a remote village in Denmark. Th ey help a French refugee who repays their years of kindness with a sumptuous feast fit for a king. Love is in full force as this small group of believers huddle together against the cold dark and learn that good food truly brings us all together. Part of the Badlands Film Appreciation Society's Foreign Views series \(bfas.art\).

events.description:
Blue Hawk Theatre Guild Presents

Junie B. Jones in Jingle Bells, Batman Smells! Get ready to kick off the holiday season with laughter, heart, and plenty of holiday cheer! Blue Hawk Theatre Guild, featuring Dickinson State University students alongside talented community members, proudly presents Junie B. Jones in Jingle Bells, Batman Smells!.

Junie B. Jones is excited about the holiday season and the Secret Santa gift exchange at school. But when she draws her class tattletale, May, as the recipient of her gift, Junie faces an important question: Will she embrace the true spirit of Christmas, kindness, and goodwill? Filled with hilarious moments, memorable characters, and an uplifting message, this family-friendly production is the perfect way to begin your holiday celebrations.

Join us Thanksgiving weekend for this festive theatrical tradition! Performance DatesFriday – Thanksgiving Weekend 7:00pm

Saturday – Thanksgiving Weekend 7:00pm

Sunday – Thanksgiving Weekend 2:00 pm

AdmissionAdults: $10

Students (K–12): $5

events.title: Junie B. in Jingle Bells, Batman Smells!
events.description:
Blue Hawk Theatre Guild Presents

Junie B. Jones in Jingle Bells, Batman Smells! Get ready to kick off the holiday season with laughter, heart, and plenty of holiday cheer! Blue Hawk Theatre Guild, featuring Dickinson State University students alongside talented community members, proudly presents Junie B. Jones in Jingle Bells, Batman Smells!.

Junie B. Jones is excited about the holiday season and the Secret Santa gift exchange at school. But when she draws her class tattletale, May, as the recipient of her gift, Junie faces an important question: Will she embrace the true spirit of Christmas, kindness, and goodwill? Filled with hilarious moments, memorable characters, and an uplifting message, this family-friendly production is the perfect way to begin your holiday celebrations.
